text:
Wall Street really convinced millions of 25-year-olds to skip Europe, drive a 2008 Corolla, and shovel every spare dollar into retirement accounts for 40 years.

Then private equity started buying the nursing homes.

Now you're 79, paying $12,000 a month to eat microwaved meatloaf under fluorescent lights while a guy named Harold screams at Wheel of Fortune.

They convinced you to save the money and then figured out how to take it all back.

Don’t call it financial planning.

name: Rachel cole
text: In the 30 days to October 5, US spot ETF flows, stablecoin growth and corporate treasury buying brought in about $4.9B. Over the same period, the Realized Cap, the value of all coins at the price they last moved, rose by about $12.8B. New money therefore covers less than two fifths of that rise. The rest is coins changing hands at higher prices among money already in the market. The rallies of 2024 and 2025 showed a similar mix, but on far larger inflows.

name: BITPRESS | Markets from Seoul
text: Bitcoin ETFs took in $1.08 billion in three days, and bitcoin still fell to $81,100. Big money sounds bullish, but ETF money has often come in after prices rose. In past rallies, about $235 million a day kept coming for months.

name: TetherBurger
text: There are reports this week that Switzerland approved its first spot bitcoin ETF for retail investors. The fund is expected to start trading on the SIX Swiss Exchange in November, holding bitcoin directly under Swiss fund law. Most listed crypto products in Europe are debt-style ETPs, so a real fund structure for retail is a notable step. Which market do you think follows?
